newsitem.title: MEXICO: Right-wing suggests cutting Mexico's bureaucracy.
newsitem.headline: Right-wing suggests cutting Mexico's bureaucracy.

text.p: Mexico's conservative National Action Party (PAN) said it will encourage the disappearance of at least two government ministries in a move to cut bureaucracy and public spending.

The new leader of the PAN's recently elected 122 lower house deputies, Francisco Paoli, told Reuters his party will look to trim red tape and promote a gradual reduction of the value added tax to 10 percent from 15 percent.

Paoli said the PAN will propose the Agricultural Reform Ministry and the Tourism Ministry be eliminated. He said Mexico has not seen agriculture reform in years and that tourism could be managed at the state level.
"We are proposing a revision and simplification of public administration," the PAN legislator-elect said.

At the July 6 mid-term vote, opposition legislators won a majority in the lower house of Congress from the long-ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) for the first time ever, and are looking forward to fierce debate when the September session begins.
